claim.pdf_says: CheckingAccount Class   (underlined, exactly as 'Account Class' is underlined on page 1144)
claim.markdown_says: CheckingAccount Class   (plain text, specs/ISO_COBOL.md - page-1145 slice line 6), whereas page 1144 renders the matching label as '<u>Account Class</u>'.
claim.why_it_matters: Purely presentational, but the two labels are a matched pair in the same example and the transcription treats them differently; a reader diffing the two code samples sees an asymmetry that is not in the standard.

verdict.reasoning:
The claim's observations are factually accurate, but the discrepancy is formatting-only and is therefore rejected under the standing rule that pure presentation differences are not content discrepancies.

What I independently confirmed by rendering the pages at 300 dpi and reading the transcription:

1. PDF p1145 (printed folio 1115), rendered to E:/Temp/specrecon/v1145/spec_p1145.png: the caption 'CheckingAccount Class' sitting above the CLASS-ID. CheckingAccount code block IS underlined. I looked at the glyphs directly - there is a continuous rule running under the full string from the 'C' of CheckingAccount through the final 's' of 'Class'.

2. PDF p1144 (printed folio 1114), rendered to E:/Temp/specrecon/v1144/spec_p1144.png: the matching caption 'Account Class' above the CLASS-ID. Account code block is likewise underlined.

3. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 46001 reads '<u>Account Class</u>' (underline preserved); line 46047, inside the page-1145 slice, reads 'CheckingAccount Class' with no <u> wrapper (underline dropped). So the asymmetry the claim describes does exist in the transcription, and it is a real drop rather than a reflow: the text itself is present, complete, correctly spelled, and on the expected line - only the <u> markup is absent.

Why this is nevertheless not a reportable content discrepancy:

- The lost underline carries no meaning. In this document underlining is semantically load-bearing in exactly one place: general formats / syntax diagrams, where an underlined word is a REQUIRED reserved word as opposed to an optional noise word (this is what the ~97 <u> occurrences elsewhere in the markdown encode, e.g. '<u>PROGRAM-ID</u>', '[ <u>NOT</u> ] boolean-expression-1'). 'CheckingAccount Class' is not a general format and contains no reserved words - it is an editorial caption naming the example that follows, in Annex D, which is informative. Underlined or not, it reads identically and implies nothing about COBOL syntax or semantics.

- No text is missing, altered, reordered, or misattributed. Nothing a compiler, a conformance test, or a rule-derivation would ever consult is affected.

- The transcription is not even uniformly wrong about these captions - it is faithful where the PDF is plain. I checked the third sibling caption: PDF p1140 (printed folio 1110) prints 'Checking Account Class' WITHOUT an underline, and specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 45869 correspondingly has it as plain text. So the converter is tracking the source styling in 2 of the 3 sibling captions and dropped it in 1; this is ordinary styling noise in the OCR/conversion pipeline, not a content defect.

- The claim's own stated impact - 'a reader diffing the two code samples sees an asymmetry' - concerns the appearance of the prose surrounding two code blocks whose contents are unaffected. That is precisely the class of difference the rejection criteria call out as formatting.

One correction to the claim's framing, offered for the record rather than as a basis for accepting it: the claim implies the pair is 'in the same example'. They are two adjacent but distinct examples (the Account class on p1144 and the CheckingAccount subclass on p1145), captioned separately; and the wider set of such captions in this annex is three, not two, the third (p1140) being un-underlined in both sources.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The claim is factually accurate as far as it goes - PDF p1145 does underline the caption 'CheckingAccount Class', and specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 46047 transcribes it as plain text while line 46001 preserves the underline on p1144's 'Account Class' - but the difference is purely presentational markup with no semantic content. Underlining is meaning-bearing in this standard only inside general formats, where it marks required reserved words; here it is an editorial caption style over a code example in informative Annex D. The caption text itself is fully present, correctly spelled, and correctly placed. Additionally, the transcription is not systematically dropping these underlines: the third sibling caption, 'Checking Account Class' on PDF p1140, is un-underlined in the PDF and correspondingly plain at markdown line 45869, so the source styling is being tracked correctly in 2 of 3 cases. Reject as formatting-only.
